research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 10855) prints Executive Order 11121 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1963-10-09; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the United Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving United Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11121 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11127, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11127 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11127
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE; BE­
TWEEN THE FLORIDA EAST COAST RAILWAY COMPANY AND CER­
TAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W H E R E AS a dispute exists between the Florida East Coast Rail­
way Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by 
the Eleven Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, designated m 
L IS T  A  attached hereto and made a part hereof; and
W H E R E AS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
W H E R E A S this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, TH E R E FO RE , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section-10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Florida East Coast Railway Company, or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11127 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11138, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11138 Modifying provisions for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations". The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03). Whether the one-person waiver was exhausted earlier by its use is not established by held evidence and is disclosed as open, not claimed.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 403) and Section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, and as Presi­
dent of the United States, it is ordered that Executive Order No. 9721 
of May 10,1946, as amended by Executive Order No. 10103 of February 
1,1950, providing for the transfer of personnel to public international 
organizations in which the U nited.  States Government participates 
be, and it is hereby, modified as follows:
The limitation in Section 1 relating to the period during which an 
employee shall be considered as on leave of absence from his employ­
ment with the Federal Government, and the limitation in Section 3(a) 
relating to the period of time from date of transfer to a public inter­
national organization during which an employee is privileged to 
exercise reemployment rights, are waived with respect to Frederick 
Strauss, and he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence 
for the period August 12, 1957, through September 16, 1962, for the 
purpose of all rights and benefits provided by Executive Order 9721, 
as amended.

By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 403) and Section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, and as Presi­
dent of the United States, it is ordered that Executive Order No. 9721 
of May 10,1946, as amended by Executive Order No. 10103 of February 
1,1950, providing for the transfer of personnel to public international 
organizations in which the U nited.  States Government participates 
be, and it is hereby, modified as follows:
The limitation in Section 1 relating to the period during which an 
employee shall be considered as on leave of absence from his employ­
ment with the Federal Government, and the limitation in Section 3(a) 
relating to the period of time from date of transfer to a public inter­
national organization during which an employee is privileged to 
exercise reemployment rights, are waived with respect to Frederick 
Strauss, and he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence 
for the period August 12, 1957, through September 16, 1962, for the 
purpose of all rights and benefits provided by Executive Order 9721, 
as amended.
L yndon  B. J ohnson

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 225) prints Executive Order 11138 as an order of the President (Lyndon B. Johnson) dated 1964-01-07; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Modifying Executive Order No., as amended by Executive Order No. 10103, providing for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations). I read the whole clause and signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers every operative sentence; I confirm it as complete. The one operative clause modifies Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order No. 10103 of February 1, 1950 (transfer of personnel to public international organizations): it waives, with respect to one named person, Frederick Strauss, the Section 1 limit on the period during which a transferred employee is treated as on leave of absence and the Section 3(a) limit on the time within which reemployment rights may be exercised, and provides that he is considered to have been on leave of absence from August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 for all rights and benefits under Executive Order 9721, as amended. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11138 Modifying provisions for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. This is a one-person waiver. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28, a waiver exhausted by performance is recorded as such only where evidence shows it was used; no held source shows whether or when Mr. Strauss exercised reemployment rights or otherwise used the waiver, so no exhaustion date or interval is claimed and the question is disclosed as open. The waiver's surviving consequence (his deemed leave status and any rights that accrued) is distinct from the permission itself. The express revocation is the first ending shown by held evidence. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception; rights that accrued to the named person before the revocation are treated as accrued, not as a continuing independent command. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11168, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11168 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11168
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY  
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Eleven Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, 
labor organizations, designated in List B attached hereto and made a 
part hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board, to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputés. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier. \
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

Executive Order 11170
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part thereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, labor 
organizations, designated in List B attached hereto and made a part 
hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10, of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 11885) prints Executive Order 11168 as an order of the President (Lyndon B. Johnson) dated 1964-08-18; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11168 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11169, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11169 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11169
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Six Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations func­
tioning through the Railway Employes’  Department, AFL-CIO, 
labor organizations, designated in the List B attached hereto and made 
a part hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree siich as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board, to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 11889) prints Executive Order 11169 as an order of the President (Lyndon B. Johnson) dated 1964-08-18; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11169 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date.
